In April, I ordered some t-shirts. Almost half of them came out wrong. The designs were altered or even reversed.

I demanded they fix them and make them correctly.

I'm asking that instead of fixing the t-shirts... I get a refund.
Before this, I left a review on Google. Until I did this... they didn't even acknowledge me. I would have continued waiting...
They're unprofessional... And if there's a problem... they ignore you.

To get a refund for the t-shirts they made wrong... they asked me to delete the previous review. (I did it just to get my money back...) I'm leaving this review here again to document what happened over three months without any solutions. I'm very angry with the treatment and the wasted time...
I DO NOT RECOMMEND THEM AT ALL.
I'm attaching photos again. For example, reversed designs...:

One star? They don't even deserve a "good morning." They're shameless and incompetent.
I waited a month in good faith for them to make me a simple t-shirt because they supposedly had a large order they couldn't ignore. So far, so good. They can't do two things at once, and that's fine. But their customer service via WhatsApp was appalling. They ignored important questions and were even arrogant and cocky at times. Since they wouldn't give me specific dates and everything was very vague, I asked them to please refund my money until the t-shirt was actually made, but they said they had already paid for the materials (the t-shirt itself), and apparently that wasn't an option either. A money they couldn't even confirm they had received, despite my asking.

To make matters worse, when the t-shirt was ready, and since they still hadn't answered my question about whether they did shipping, I traveled to the other side of Madrid (I had to ask a relative for help) to pick it up at their warehouse during the business hours they'd told me. Surprise, surprise, nobody was there. When I called them, the person I spoke to still had the nerve to respond arrogantly and insist they were right. The solution they offered was...to send me the t-shirt. Because, well, it turns out they do shipping. How stupid of me not to know that and to have gone all the way there for nothing! Oh, wait, they didn't give me that information when I asked them. That was on Monday, and they were supposed to send the t-shirt the next day, which should have arrived yesterday. As of Thursday, I still haven't received anything, and they haven't contacted me to update me or anything like that. When I write to them and ask for an order tracking number or something...what do I find? Guess what... THEY'RE COMPLETELY IGNORING ME. They're not answering my messages or calls anymore.
It's unbelievable what these people are doing because for me to leave a review like this, things must have been seriously, seriously wrong. It's time to stop taking people for fools like this.
If you don't know how to run a business, stick to selling badges. Or if you like making fun of people, start making hidden camera videos. Blessings.

one_star_reviews.text: I'm really disappointed with this company. They initially approved our car loan, so we made a deposit. To our surprise, they then told us the loan had been denied, which was a huge shock because they had already said it was approved. So, for obvious reasons, we asked for a refund of the deposit (€350), and they haven't responded at all. They keep saying that Ivan, the finance manager, never answers or doesn't have time, and that was almost three months ago. I'm still waiting for my money back.

I hope my review is taken into account by everyone who goes to Ocasión Plus. I bought a car with a premium warranty (which they shoehorned in) and it took them a full year—yes, exactly a year—to repair the hidden defects. Four workshop managers, registered letters, consumer complaints, countless salespeople fired, lost cases, emails, calls... Their quality and warranty management is absolutely fraudulent. What the employees have to put up with for a paycheck is unbelievable... lying is a constant in this company's practices. The best thing about them, and I want to give a special mention for their work and human qualities, is Nahia from administration, Unai from the workshop, and Manu, the workshop manager. I hope you get paid what you deserve and more.

My experience with Ocasión Plus has been very disappointing.

The salesperson who helped me was Jaime. When I went to buy the car, he told me that even though it was coming from San Sebastián, it would be ready in just two days because they were going to prepare it. I trusted that the vehicle would be delivered properly inspected.

When I picked up the car, I immediately noticed that the **fourth gear was difficult to engage and made an unusual noise**. I reported it immediately, and an independent mechanic recommended that I not continue using it until it was inspected.

Furthermore, the delivery paperwork indicates that the **AdBlue level** had been checked, even though I was later told that this model doesn't even have that system. This makes me doubt the inspection that was carried out before delivery.

I left the vehicle on a Saturday because the salesperson assured me that the inspection would begin on Monday and that I would have it back that same week. However, the deadlines have kept changing, and I still don't have a clear solution. One day I was even told that the gearbox probably just needed lubrication and that I could take the car. However, another dealership employee specifically advised against it, saying that if I took the car and continued driving it, it could break down further, and the dealership could then blame the damage on my use of the vehicle. Therefore, he advised me to leave it there until it was inspected.

I also haven't received a replacement vehicle. I've been told this is because I didn't purchase an extended warranty, an option that, in my case, was never offered to me during the purchase, and I have witnesses to this.

I've already filed the corresponding complaint, and now I just hope the dealership acts with the necessary speed and professionalism to resolve the issue.

I must say that Nahia is a wonderful woman and the only one who offered me a solution. Thank you so much, and congratulations to her!

Update: Today I received a call from customer service saying that the salesperson isn't obligated to provide the warranties. I asked them if that's the case, and they deliver a broken vehicle without prior inspection, how is it possible that they won't give me a replacement car? It's clearly their fault.

I'm not giving it zero stars because I can't. The salesman who helped us, Jaime, was wonderful when he was selling us the car, but once he sold it to us with problems, he disappeared. A horrible experience.

I don't recommend buying from them. After the sale, they wash their hands of all responsibility; you're left to fix things yourself. I've been waiting five months for a response regarding a warranty, and in the end, I've had to fix it myself. To sum it up, they're not just bad, they're perverse.
A disaster

one_star_reviews.text: Where to begin… At first, everything is smooth sailing until you pay for the car and then they completely ignore you. I bought a 2019 Seat Leon almost two months ago, and the only time I've driven it was the day I picked it up from the dealership. The day we went to see the car, it was covered in cans and dirt from having driven it; they didn't even bother to clean it, even though they knew we were coming that day. I brought the car back the following week, and shortly after leaving the dealership, the engine light came on and the revs were limited, making it somewhat dangerous to drive (photo 1). I sent them a photo, and they told me that didn't indicate a problem 😂 (photo 2). What's going on? Do they sometimes limit cars just because they feel like it? Anyway, I took it to the garage, and the result: low turbocharger/replace turbo (photo 3). I contacted the warranty department and they told me they had to give me a rebuilt, exchange turbocharger, not a new one because it's a used car—unbelievable. They sent it to me after sending me the wrong address, and a week had already passed. When they were about to install it, they told me it was better to drain the oil because it was already black. I told the mechanics that the dealership had told me it had been changed along with the filter, and they sent me this video (video 1). The oil, if they supposedly changed it, had 300 km on it, and with that mileage, you wouldn't find it like that in a gasoline car, not a chance. They installed the turbocharger and we went to test it, and everything seemed fine. The next day I went for a drive in my car, and at first, it was great. After a while, a bunch of warning lights came on (photo 4). I'm editing my review.
Stellantis hasn't responded to my claim after three months. They contacted me to ask me to provide them with the in-court document (apud acta) online using a digital certificate.

I don't have a digital certificate, so I asked if there was any other way to obtain one. I waited two weeks and they gave me two options: pay a representative or go to the courthouse in person.

I don't have time to go to the courthouse during office hours because of work, and I've already paid €395 upfront and received terrible service from them.

I filed another claim for a different car at the same time with RECLAMATUCOCHE.COM. They refunded part of my money in two months without me having to pay anything upfront.

If you want good service and peace of mind, stay away from this company. On top of charging upfront, they abandon you.

I have to tell anyone thinking of using Corpe Legal's services not to. At first, everything seems to go quickly, but after paying them and after almost six months, they don't answer the phone or inform you about the status of your claim. I think this looks like a scam because I feel cheated.

Hello, I contacted them yesterday. Ines was very attentive and informed me of everything. I will make the provision of funds in a few days and file two lawsuits for the financed vehicle. I have complete confidence in them and hope everything goes smoothly.

Today, June 30th, I still haven't heard anything about my appraisal. It doesn't matter if you call or not; the appraiser doesn't have it yet. Of course, he has so much work and so many contracts that it will take a year, and then it will go to court. Lately, they haven't answered. I have two lawsuits filed. The manufacturer appealed the €1200 fees that Elois charged him. Since they haven't resolved our case, they haven't paid me the €400 they are owed. And keep in mind that my claim is for €6500, so they are the ones who win.

At first they answer any questions... but after you pay the €300 they just relax... I've been waiting for over a year... what a waste of time and money... So if you have time and money to spare, hire this company 🤮🤮🤮🤮 …

Since June 2025, I've been religiously paying for the process, and after numerous conversations with Coral, they always tell me everything is underway. When I follow up again after a few months, Coral stops responding. Emails go unanswered, and miraculously, they recently told me to complete the "Apudacta" procedure, or if I prefer, for a little extra money, they'll do it for me. Basically, it's a cash grab. The thing is, I handled the process myself and sent them the Apudacta in PDF format as instructed, and after that, about a month ago, nothing. They don't answer WhatsApp messages, emails, or anything. Logically, the lawsuit should be processed within 3-4 months of the initial payment. Are we going to fight with Banco Santander or with you at Corpe Legal?

Edit: 2nd time, June 22, 2026:
They just sent me an email terminating the contract, citing a clause that is a LIE. I've attached the clause they're using to KEEP MY DEPOSIT, as well as the conversation confirming that I notified them and they told me to send the documentation.

Edit: June 22, 2026:
I just received a call from the firm, very subtly pressuring me to remove the review because otherwise they "will manage my deposit in another way." During the call, the person on the other end told me I was defaming them by calling them shameless and discrediting them. According to my lawyer, calling them shameless is a personal value judgment, which I can freely and publicly express. It's a different matter, for example, if I were to call them "swindlers," which would obviously be a lie.

On the other hand, to publicly demonstrate that I am simply sharing my experience and that it is true, and that it's not that I want to terminate the contract but rather that they are the ones failing to fulfill their obligations, and therefore I have the right to withdraw and recover all of my deposit, which I paid 14 months ago and with the case still unresolved, I am attaching the conversations.

They are utterly shameless. I contacted them to claim back the exorbitant interest on a car loan, and they told me the process would be resolved in 8 or 9 months. According to the timeline they provided, it should have been resolved by December 2025 or January at the latest. In October of that same year, I consolidated that loan with another one, as they told me there wouldn't be a problem claiming back because the original loan would be canceled since it was paid off, and that the interest could still be claimed. They kept me on the back burner for almost a month because, after calling to ask beforehand since it was cheaper for me, they kept telling me that some lawyers said yes and others said no. So I sent them all the documentation they requested again, and I was surprised because they couldn't figure out what the problem was, given that they had already given me the go-ahead beforehand, and they had even issued me a new loan, which didn't mention anywhere that it was a debt consolidation loan. After a few weeks of waiting, they told me they would file a claim with the finance company without any problem, delaying the process by a couple of months since that's the time the finance company has to respond to the claim. The last time I spoke with them, in April, they said they would call me the following week to let me know if they had filed the lawsuit, and I'm still waiting. I've written to them several times and haven't received any response. It's been over a year since I paid them the initial deposit. I understand that the process has been delayed two months due to the reunification, but even if the process had started completely over, it should already be resolved within the expected timeframe of 8 to 9 months. I bought a vehicle in April of this year. A 2014 Audi A1. (I hope they don't claim this is a fake review, as I have proof of purchase and a signed contract). I've waited all this time to post this review to see if the problem would be resolved, but they take a long time to respond and often give me the runaround.
Personally, I can't leave a positive review. The salesperson's service and attention were very good, but the car has hidden defects:

1. Side impact damage not fully repaired. They told me they were going to repair a small scratch, but they left it as is. A dent in the rocker panel that isn't visible at first glance. It's structural damage. It's misaligned (hidden defect). I've attached a photo.

2. Vibration in the steering wheel at certain speeds.

Their after-sales service takes a long time to respond, and as usual, they give you the runaround. They claim that because the vehicle is over X years old and you had it inspected by them, you're stuck with the defects.

I didn't have a good buying experience with StreetCar.

Almost a year ago, my partner and I decided to buy a car from StreetCar. First of all, I recommend checking if the car has a service booklet. Ours didn't, and it was a big mistake not to notice it earlier. That booklet is essential for knowing the car's history, what repairs were done, and what kind of care it received. At the end of the sale, before leaving the dealership, Hernandez suggested (several times) that we leave a 5-star review. I decided to wait… and thank goodness, because the after-sales service was very disappointing. Warning lights started appearing on the dashboard saying "Engine Fault" less than two weeks after we bought it. It took almost four months of diagnoses and back-and-forth trips to repair shops before they finally agreed to take responsibility. The car has to be taken to their workshop, which is 50 minutes from Madrid—super inconvenient. Supposedly, the purchase includes a warranty for hidden defects, which is precisely for these situations, right? If the fault appears within a few days, it's clearly not the buyer's fault. We reported it immediately because from the very beginning I wanted to make it clear that if this problem wasn't resolved properly, we wouldn't want the car. Regardless of whether the warranty covered it or not, the important thing for me was to make it clear that a car with engine problems wasn't what we had bought.

When we were using the car and this alert appeared, the system went into Malfunction Mode, forcing us to abruptly reduce our speed. It's a dangerous situation that shouldn't happen. They repaired it (or so I want to believe), but two days after picking up the car from their workshop, the fault reappeared. We tried to get lawyers and file a complaint with consumer protection so they wouldn't get away with it. We knew we wouldn't achieve much, because it's a tedious process, but it was worth trying.

I absolutely do not recommend this place to anyone; they are very dishonest. It took ages to get a response from them; I had to chase them down everywhere for months, always being incredibly polite in the hope that they would finally take responsibility and because I knew that otherwise they would just stop replying. Even so, they never fixed the engine problem.

The after-sales manager at Gestican Los Majuelos told me that I had to pay for the parts and that they would cover the labor, meaning I have to pay around €280 for the sensors since he says the warranty doesn't cover electronic components. Until I realized that the rear seatbelts didn't lock or retract. I notified them, and they referred me to the after-sales manager in Tenerife, a guy named Carlos.

one_star_reviews.text: Hello, I bought a vehicle from this company in December 2025. The first thing I told them was that I was from out of town, that I was interested in the car, and that if, in their opinion, it was in the condition advertised, I would buy it. I asked for honesty above all else, as after other bad experiences, I was a bit tired of having problems with cars. In this case, Rubén told me that the car was in very good condition, that it had up-to-date maintenance on both the engine and the gearbox, and that the car ran like a dream. For my part, which was a big mistake on my part, I trusted his words, the videos, and the information he gave me, and I bought the car right away. Two months later, due to circumstances, I decided to sell the car, and before doing so, I hired a company to give it a thorough inspection. After this inspection, manipulation was detected in the engine's operating hours compared to the operating hours of the gearbox and other modules. The diagnostic equipment detected, during a check of various modules, that the car's windshield was calibrated in 2016, registering a mileage of 164,000 km during that calibration. It also revealed that the vehicle's impact protection modules had been activated on two separate occasions, due to side and roof impacts. I purchased the car in December 2025 with 166,000 km (according to the odometer), and upon becoming aware of all this, I contacted them. Because we were within the legal warranty period covered by consumer law, I demanded the cancellation of the vehicle purchase. One of their many responses was that I must have caused the accident myself and now I want to sue them, that I should file a complaint, that the car was in perfect condition, considering they didn't even bother to change the air filter… In short, it's surreal and there's no solution whatsoever. They're turning a deaf ear to everything, and I'm stuck with it. Thanks to our legal system, I'll just have to wait and wait, only to end up in the same situation. If this ever happens to you with these people, don't even bother trying to reach an agreement or claiming what's in the contract. It's a waste of time. If you have the patience and the ability to wait and pursue legal action, fine. Otherwise, you'll end up like me: paying for the car and dealing with a huge mess.

Terrible experience with the BYD Atto 3 Evo Excellence and appalling sales and technical service.

Having driven brands like Mercedes, BMW, and Tesla, I can say without hesitation that this is the worst car I've ever owned. The purchase experience and the vehicle itself have been a complete rip-off compared to what I was promised.

I was assisted by the salesman David, who sold me this model as a superior option to any other on the market, highlighting a series of features that have turned out to be false:

* "Impressive" connectivity: They promised advanced connectivity but offer a ridiculously low 1 GB data plan. Just the automatic download of offline maps (which can't even be disabled) consumes around 600 MB. With any other basic car function, the data is used up instantly. To make matters worse, after a certain period, they expect you to pay a monthly subscription for a useless service.

* Fake Google Automotive and terrible navigation: I was sold a "Google Automotive" system that, in practice, doesn't work. There's no data correlation between the car and the navigation app, so planning charging stops along the route is practically nonexistent, completely failing to deliver on what was promised during the sales process.

* Lack of promised features: I was assured of features like sentry mode and full remote control from the mobile app (location, climate control, etc.) that are not what was promised.

To top it all off, the customer service and after-sales support are disastrous:

* Exorbitant charges: After only 4 months, the battery in the second remote (which I hadn't even used) completely died. Instead of covering it as a courtesy or warranty after a recent purchase, they charged me €12.10 for a battery that costs between €1 and €3 anywhere else.

* Lack of technical knowledge: I've had to take the car to the shop twice, and it seems that even the brand's own technicians are unfamiliar with the operating system and how this new model works.

If BYD doesn't provide me with an immediate solution that meets my needs, I will formally file a lawsuit for false advertising and submit a complaint to the consumer protection agency.

one_star_reviews.text: Two years after the delivery of Celere Kentia, we still have no solution to the swimming pool (closed due to countless leaks) and other problems such as dampness in the storage room, walls of the house, etc.

An endless nightmare: Vía Célere crosses all legal and ethical boundaries with its customers.
• If you're thinking of buying a home with Vía Célere, I advise you to think twice. My experience with them has been a complete disaster, marked by negligent after-sales service that has dragged on for over a year. Once you sign and hand over the money, they completely abandon you.

• The treatment I received has exceeded all legal and ethical limits for customer service. They left me with a long list of unrepaired defects, which they completely disclaim responsibility for. Faced with their silence and lack of solutions, I was forced to resort to their ethics channel, send registered letters, and pay out of my own pocket to hire independent professionals (such as glaziers) to certify the damages they refuse to take responsibility for.

• • Among the defects they refuse to repair are factory defects in the glass (deep scratches), poor paint finishes, and damage to woodwork caused by mishandling of materials during construction. Their response is always the same: to decline responsibility.

• The most critical and distressing situation I experienced was directly with the head of the glass/PVC department and the subcontracted staff. Their intervention in my home not only failed to resolve anything, but they also directly damaged interior materials. This extreme negligence and lack of professionalism rendered my home uninhabitable for months, causing me an unacceptable level of stress and anxiety.

• Vía Célere does not honor the warranty on its developments nor take responsibility for the damage caused by its workers. I leave this review as a warning to future buyers: after-sales service is nonexistent, they evade their legal responsibilities, and systematic mistreatment of customers is their standard operating procedure. Don't be fooled by the initial treatment at the sales booth.

Shameful. As another commenter said: the friendliness vanishes the moment you sign the contract. The saleswoman, whom we all know, goes on and on about how great the property is, but then don't even bother asking her for information about anything. They won't even open the office door. RUDE, DISHONEST. I don't know how they sleep at night. And the after-sales service is just as bad. The house is terribly built, with obvious and appalling flaws; even my young son can see the problems... BUT THEY DON'T. They close the case on the app with excuses for idiots. No, Vía Célere... we work hard to pay for a home (with honest jobs) and we shouldn't be left with such awful issues unresolved...

Zero solutions and a complete lack of effort to fix construction defects, especially hidden flaws.

In my neighborhood, Jacaranda, they've left numerous defects unresolved. Here's a brief summary:

- Uninstalled lawn; we residents had to pay for artificial turf.

- Water leak in the pool; we residents had to pay for its repair.

- Poor wiring for the driveway lights; it's currently being inspected by an expert, as they indicate it was tampered with by the maintenance contractor.

- The perimeter wall of the facade has cracks and large pieces have fallen off. I urge anyone considering buying a home from Vía Celere to take a walk around the outside of the development.

Vía Celere's response to the residents has been that it's due to slamming doors.

- There are faults in the fiber optic cable running from the RITI (Telecommunications Infrastructure Room) to many of the homes. Each home was reported in 2023, and the solution provided was not permanent. The cable continued to malfunction for some time until it finally stopped working altogether. The matter has been referred to an expert.

- Dampness inside the homes, even inside closets, causing damage to the closets and deteriorating the residents' clothing.

I will never buy another home from them, nor will I recommend them to family and friends looking for housing in the Entrenúcleos area.

Regards.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm giving it one star because there aren't any negative ones.
My mother was at this center for two and a half months, and everything went terribly wrong. It's an administrative disaster with an incredible lack of staff.
The medical reports submitted upon admission were lost, or so I was told. I want to believe that's what happened, not that they acted in bad faith. (How is it possible to lose them?) Each resident is supposed to have a file with their medical history.
As for the clothing, it was poorly organized in the closets, all the clothes were labeled, and on more than one occasion, she was wearing clothes that weren't hers.
When she left the center, two shirts, a pair of pants, and a nightgown were missing; the nightgown never turned up.
Regarding the financial aspect, I had to request a refund of the deposit for her place several times, and the same thing happened with the days my mother didn't use during her stay. After waiting 20 days, I finally received the money after I told them I was going to report the matter to the Madrid Community Consumer Protection Office.

I chose this residence because I believed it offered some of the best conditions for residents at a reasonable price, sacrificing the distance for visits.

The problem lies in the healthcare, which leaves much to be desired. The medication and its dispensing are poorly controlled, and there's a risk of causing health problems for the residents. The worst part is that they tell you they can understand if you want to move to another residence, when logically they should be focused on preventing errors and improving the service.
As for the staff, in general, they strive to do their job well, although there's too much staff turnover. I hope this review helps improve the service because I believe it's a good residence.

I'm editing this review to lower the star rating. The services initially contracted are gradually being discontinued. They started with the physiotherapist, now the doctor, and the dining room. I'm expanding the review because if anything could get worse, it is. With the holidays upon us, the staff shortage is worrying. They're practically doing nothing, without providing adequate hygiene for the residents, and on top of that, telling them they have to dress themselves. And the food is getting worse and worse. We may not have received an email informing us that they're going to adjust the monthly cost to the actual service provided, but that wouldn't be the solution because it's not about paying less, but about receiving adequate service at all times, not depending on the staff they have.
Our elderly residents and we ourselves make a great effort to ensure they are as comfortable as possible.
I hope the owners of the residence take measures to ensure that the service they provide is what was contracted and not a deception that increasingly harms the residents.
I'm editing this comment to note that the food service has become abysmal, to the point of causing anemia in some residents. It's a shame that the management is so incompetent, ignoring the residents' written complaints about the food. I can't recommend this residence at all.

And now they're breaking the contract and raising prices as they see fit, without any agreement or justification. It'll be for buying towels, for example, because they take them off in the morning and put them back on whenever they remember, and if they complain, either there aren't any or the washing machine isn't working. Let's see if they respond and justify why they're breaching the contract. Maybe they'll even convince us while we refund the payments for breach of contract?

The residence is visually appealing, with new, spacious, and bright facilities. They advertise occupational therapy for residents, a gym with a physiotherapist and doctor. However, the reality is that there's a staff shortage. Only a small minority of elderly residents who attend occupational therapy are independent and have no cognitive problems; the rest are neglected and spend their time sitting in front of the television. There's no physiotherapy, and they don't take the elderly residents down to the gym, even though they see it could benefit them. The residence doesn't respond to complaints or requests via email; they reply late and don't resolve anything. My relative's clothes are often dirty, and they lack hygiene when I visit. No one supervises them, even though they can shower on their own afterward. They don't monitor bathing days or when they change their clothes. My relative showed up one week with edema in their legs, something very noticeable that no one had seen. There's absolutely no supervision from the staff or the doctor. Residents with better memories speak very badly of the food. There's a garden, treeless, where it's impossible to go outside in the summer, but it doesn't matter because they never take the residents out, even just to play and get some sun. Little care is given to the elderly; it's all just for show. I'm considering moving soon. It's poorly located, too far from public transport.

My experience at this care home has been very negative. There is a clear lack of staff, which directly impacts the care residents receive. There are not enough staff to adequately attend to the basic needs of the elderly, and this affects the quality of service.

There is also a noticeable lack of organization and staff at reception, which makes communication with families difficult. The quality of the food leaves much to be desired, and the cleanliness is not what one would expect in a center intended for the care of vulnerable people.

The lack of basic supplies is particularly worrying. There are not enough bibs for all the residents who need them, and old, worn, or torn towels are used. All of this conveys a sense of neglect and lack of care in fundamental aspects.

In my mother's case, a perfume and a cushion disappeared from her room. We reported what happened to the care home, but we did not receive a satisfactory solution, nor was any responsibility taken for the loss of these items.

I also find it concerning that residents with severe cognitive impairments live alongside other residents without sufficient supervision at all times. This situation can lead to conflict, discomfort, and insecurity.

Older adults deserve dignified care, clean and well-maintained facilities, and services tailored to their needs. Unfortunately, my experience at this residence has been very disappointing.

Therefore, I do not recommend this residence to anyone looking for a care home for a family member. My advice is to visit and consider other options before making such an important decision.

I visited this place with friends and was extremely disappointed. I ordered a hookah with "premium tobacco" for €25, but they used regular Al Fakher, with a very weak and indistinct flavor. The hookah itself produced almost no smoke and was completely unsatisfying.

I honestly don't understand how this place got such high ratings. The atmosphere looks rather tired and unkempt, but the main thing for a hookah bar is the hookah, and that's where things get really bad.

I was particularly surprised to see the staff smoking their own hookah at the time, which was thickly smoky and, apparently, much better prepared. The entire room was filled with smoke from their hookah, while the quality they serve to their guests was completely different. Apparently, they don't make bad hookahs for themselves.

Personally, I won't be coming back here again and can't recommend this place.

After many years as a customer, you eventually understand how trust works... but only in one direction.
For years they've had all my information, I've left my vehicle with them, and there's never been a single problem with payments. When they present me with an invoice for almost €1,000 in labor, they don't show me how many hours they've worked, what each mechanic did exactly, or how they divided that time. I simply trust that the work done and the billing are correct. That's the foundation of any trusting relationship between a customer and their garage.

However, when it comes to them trusting a long-time customer, the story changes completely.

After accepting an increased estimate from €1,600 to €2,400 because "the diesel pump is leaking," without seeing a single photo or any proof, enduring a delay in delivery without any information, and making the payment as soon as they told me to, I went to the dealership with proof of the transfer, and even then they held my vehicle for over four hours because "the money hadn't yet appeared in their account." Neither my history as a customer, nor the bank statement, nor the fact that I had always fulfilled my obligations mattered at all.

Trust, it seems, only works when it benefits the garage.
The most ironic thing is that to charge almost €1,000 for labor, all they have to do is ask the customer for a leap of faith. But when it comes to delivering a vehicle to a customer who has trusted them for years and provides proof of payment with a bank statement, that same faith completely vanishes. A business relationship based on unilateral distrust ceases to be a relationship of trust. And when a loyal customer discovers that their word is worth less than the automatic refresh of a bank account, it's difficult to continue recommending the service.

I got married a month ago and I'm still waiting for my deposit (point 4 below). The venue is beautiful, but my experience with Finca Azahares' event management has been very disappointing. My recommendation is to carefully review the contract before booking.

1 - Nobody tells you that certain things aren't allowed; you wouldn't know unless the caterer (who is external to the venue) contacted you. For example, you can't put a cocktail bar, a sofa, a photo booth, etc., on the lawn. I had to change my wedding layout the day before.

2 - When you want to store things the day before, there's no suitable private place to do so. When I arrived, the cleaning lady told me to store my things (decorations and such) in an outside room, but the owner arrived, saw me, and made me move everything. Where? To a bathroom that has a lock, but it's a bathroom, and therefore small and not suitable or adapted for storing things. Your other option is to leave it in the living room where everyone can touch or see what you've brought.

3 - You have to collect your things the same day; at most, you can lock them in the bathroom. That is, at 6:00 a.m., when my wedding ended, I had to start clearing tables and other items I had brought because the cleaner told me everything had to be clean for them to return my deposit.

4 - A month after the celebration, I still haven't received my deposit back or a written response to the emails in which I requested an explanation. During the celebration, a guest caused an incident while intoxicated outside the venue, in the driveway where other people's vehicles were parked. I cooperated fully with them to resolve the incident, and later, a guest told me that he tried to call the police immediately, but the cleaner told him not to. And although the venue was left in perfect condition, to this day I still haven't received my deposit back. I have requested in writing that they provide the exact reason for withholding my security deposit and the contract clause on which they base this decision, and a month has passed, and I still haven't received a response.

What disappoints me most is not only the situation with the deposit, but also that, after sending two emails in the last month requesting a written explanation, I haven't received any reply.

I hope this situation can be resolved, and I will update this review if I receive a response or a solution from the property.

My intention with this review is to share my experience so that other couples have all the information before booking.

I requested a financing proposal from the Ebro Autocam dealership (Vilafranca del Penedès) and noticed that it included, by default, a life insurance policy exceeding €1,500, even though the document itself stated it was optional. In my case, I already have a life insurance policy with a substantial coverage amount, which is perfectly valid for transferring rights to the financial institution, making any additional policy unnecessary. However, when I asked for this insurance to be removed from the proposal, I was told that they "couldn't remove it" because it was supposedly part of the purchase conditions, contradicting what the document explicitly states.

This contradiction raises reasonable doubts about the clarity and legality of the practice, as well as about a possible financial incentive to formalize policies not requested by the customer.

I'm sharing this information so other buyers are aware that financing offers may include insurance policies listed as mandatory, even when the customer already has fully valid policies to cover the transaction. Carefully reviewing each document is essential to avoid redundant costs or incorrect terms.

My experience with Alicante City Hall has been very disappointing.

I've been trying to complete a procedure for over two months, and during all this time, different officials and officers have given me contradictory information. Each person told me a different procedure, resulting in a constant waste of time.

The situation reached the point where an officer told me I had to pay €40 to obtain a document. After making the payment, I was informed at the police station that the document wasn't necessary and that the information I had received was incorrect. They recommended I request a refund.

More than a month has passed since I filed the request, and I still haven't received any response. What's most worrying is that the City Hall itself tells me that response times can take up to three months, which is difficult to understand in a public administration that should be at the service of the citizens (not others).

Furthermore, the website is unclear and makes it extremely difficult to carry out procedures and obtain reliable information.

I don't question the work of all the professionals in the administration, but I do believe there is a serious problem with coordination, citizen service, and efficiency. Alicante deserves more streamlined public services, consistent information, and a greater focus on resolving the problems of those who fund them with their taxes.

I hope this situation will lead to real improvements in the service and management of municipal procedures.

We booked and paid over €50 extra for this service to expedite vehicle collection, avoid unnecessary waiting, and ensure a quick and easy process—especially important since we were traveling on a tight schedule with a pre-established itinerary.

In other words, we paid a considerable amount for a benefit we did not receive.

It is unacceptable for a company to market a premium service and charge a significant surcharge without guaranteeing its proper functioning or offering an effective alternative solution when a problem arises. This situation demonstrates a complete lack of organization and consideration for customers.

I consider this practice highly unprofessional and creates a clear sense of deception, as you pay for speed and convenience that you ultimately don't receive. It was a very negative experience that, unfortunately, will make me seriously reconsider using Goldcar's services again in the future.

It gets worse when returning the car. I was very careful to return the car with 80% battery as requested. When I left the car parked it was at 80%. Then by email I am notified of a €60 charge. I quickly rush back to the office and ask to check the car. It is now parked in a different place, and miraculously, the charge now stands at 79%. I can only assume that they drove the car around the car park to run down the battery in order to make this charge.

So, for a €40 car rental I end up paying €85 - more than double the rental fee - in extra charges. I'd rather pay more upfront to rent from somewhere more reputable in future.

It was 11pm I was with my two small daughters, they kept trying to upsell me until they found an excuse to not give me the car, I didn’t get any sort of refund I was even insulted by multiple staff members. I wished I had seen the reviews before booking. This company is terrible and has no regard for their customers

UPDATE: I took the case to arbitration and won. I encourage everyone not to give up and always file a complaint and claim through official channels! (Keep all receipts!)

THIEVES! One month after the rental ended, they tried to steal €867 (!) from me for something completely fabricated (towing, etc., even though the car was returned in perfect condition). The parking staff were rude. I will NEVER, EVER rent from this company again.
Avoid at all costs. 100% of the time. Imagine the worst-case scenario and multiply it by 100. Never again.

A very bad experience with this agency.
My driver's license was refused on the spot, even though I had tried to confirm the situation beforehand with the company I had booked with.
The information they provided was contradictory, even misleading, and the staff offered no concrete help in finding a solution.
As a result, I found myself in a very difficult situation when it came time to pick up the vehicle, without any real assistance, and I was forced to book another rental elsewhere, much more expensive, at the last minute.
I strongly advise against using this agency due to its lack of transparency, its absence of customer service, and the way it leaves customers to fend for themselves once a problem arises.

RENTING WITH GOLDCAR IS AN EXPERIENCE I WILL NEVER REPEAT
Terrible experience with Goldcar at Barcelona Airport. I would never rent from them again.
We were given an SUV with multiple scratches, visible dents, and over 115,000 km on it. The worst part happened during our trip: while driving, the car displayed a low oil warning. After checking, it was missing approximately 1.5 liters of oil, which is extremely serious for a rental vehicle.
We tried contacting roadside assistance, but the phone number provided was out of service. In other words, there was no real assistance available in case of an emergency.
After many emails, the only solution offered was to drive to another airport located one hour away. Once there, the replacement options were ridiculous: either downgrade from our SUV to a Fiat 500 or pay more than €300 extra for a van.
Poorly maintained vehicles, nonexistent roadside assistance, and very poor customer service. Completely unacceptable.
They won't return my €120 gas deposit and all they do is make excuses and blame the bank. It's been over a month since they should have refunded me. They're scammers.

Very bad experience with Goldcar Barcelona.

I rented an electric Fiat 500 from Goldcar Barcelona. The experience was bad from the very beginning. At pickup, the staff member was rude and unpleasant. She pressured me about the electric car battery level and said that I could be charged a penalty if I returned the car below the required battery level. This created unnecessary stress before the rental even started.

At return, Goldcar charged me almost EUR 300 for a small missing plastic cover/trim near the front left door handle/key area. This was not an accident and not damage caused by me. The part was already missing when I collected the vehicle.

I am not a mechanic and I am not responsible for verifying the vehicle’s factory configuration or knowing whether every small plastic trim/cover should be present according to the manufacturer. Goldcar is responsible for documenting the vehicle’s condition correctly at pickup. A customer should not be charged for a small pre-existing missing plastic cover that Goldcar failed to record properly.

The employee inspected the car extremely thoroughly at return and then marked this small missing plastic part as damage. Goldcar even sent me an “accident report” request, although there was no accident, no collision, no third-party vehicle, no police report and no incident during my rental.

I disputed the charge and sent my own photo/video evidence from pickup. After that, Goldcar admitted in writing that the damage already existed prior to my rental and refunded the charge.

However, because of Goldcar’s incorrect charge, I still lost money on bank conversion/processing. Even after the refund, I was left with a financial loss caused by Goldcar’s mistake.

In my opinion, this was an unfair damage charge for a pre-existing missing part. Be extremely careful with this company: take detailed photos and videos of every tiny part of the car before leaving the parking area, including door handles, trims, wheels, bumpers and mirrors.

We rented a small car. Upon arrival, we were offered an upgrade for €5 per day, so €25 in total. In the end, we still had to pay €66. Even though we had already paid €41 for the small car.

Upon returning, we inquired about this; apparently, the upgrade was €10 per day. So, we were scammed.
If the upgrade was €10 per day, we would never have done this for 5 days. But of course, we have no proof that €5 was mentioned, so we can forget about the money.
Despite the bad reviews, we still wanted to give it a try. Unfortunately, we too fell victim to this scamming company. Never again.

Very disappointing experience with this hire car company. I was charged for damage that was either pre-existing or not clearly proven, and the process felt unfair and one-sided. Customer service was unhelpful when I tried to challenge it, leaving me frustrated and out of pocket. I strongly recommend taking detailed photos before and after your rental and arranging independent insurance with another provider, as relying on theirs may not protect you from questionable charges.

It happened again this sunday. We tried to collect our rental but were rebuffed by the goldcar desk.

He was really having a go at us. I was not going to this, because I thought it was a minor glitz. But this man did not take the course in de-escalation, or that the customer is king.
Lucky for us that the company that was the intermediary, Rental Cars, reimbursed us completely. I hope that they discontinue their affiliation with Goldcar. I hope that they take disciplinary action against this nincompoop. What a disgrace!

one_star_reviews.text: It's not like there aren't any toilets in a place that belongs to all citizens; if there aren't any, they should be installed, that's what we pay for.

It's pathetic that you contribute to social security for over 40 years, you don't get anything, and then on the day you retire you have to queue like sheep outside the door before 8 a.m., literally. At 9 a.m., a security guard comes out and rudely ushers you in to a machine to get an appointment. So far, there's no sign of any civil servants. I understand that the security personnel aren't trained for this kind of thing; they're there for what they are: security. At the very least, there should be a civil servant to advise you on what kind of consultation you need. You go in there and you're on your own. I hope they sort out my retirement and I never have to go back there again.

one_star_reviews.text:
ABSOLUTE WARNING: DO NOT HIRE CNLPRO. Our residential renovation with this company was a complete nightmare, resulting in massive pricing disputes, severe property damage, and a complete breakdown of trust.

Pricing & Transparency Issues: Quotes were left intentionally vague, resulting in essential work being charged as "extras" later. They tried to charge us €8,500 for tiles that the supplier priced at €1,900. When we confronted them about this massive markup and asked to see their original supplier quote, they flatly refused to show it to us.

Severe Safety Hazards: They left live copper wires frayed and sticking completely out of wall plugs, calling it "proper" when asked to fix it. Uncovered wires were left hanging everywhere, creating a severe physical hazard. They claimed the building lacked ground wires to excuse not installing them before closing walls. When proven wrong, they refused to fix it without extra charges, claiming electrical safety was not included in the quote.

Poor Workmanship & Damage: They punched holes through walls and sloppily slapped on random, mismatched paint. They pinched our AC condensation pipes during relocation, ruined our intercom, and refused to fix it. Fixtures and standard plugs were installed incorrectly in wrong locations without consultation; they refused to fix them, claiming they "never worked with the brand before."

Unprofessional Conduct on Site: Workers used our personal supplies and tools without permission. Several of our items were discarded or went missing, including irreplaceable bricks designated for wall repairs. They frequently did not show up to the site for a week at a time. Workers treated our unfinished property like an ashtray, chain-smoking inside and discarding cigarette butts directly onto our raw wooden parquet flooring.

Project Abandonment & Management: When called out on the unacceptable craftsmanship and pricing, they weaponized the term "hostile work environment" to terminate the project mid-renovation. They abandoned the site, leaving a half-disassembled staircase and active electrical hazards behind. We paid for end-of-work cleaning, but they left the flat a total mess, sending us a list of product recommendations instead of actually cleaning it. The supervisor visited rarely and disregarded client specifications, while the project manager offered zero coordination and only served to defend the company's unacceptable practices.

CONCLUSION: This is a highly unprofessional company with terrible business and pricing practices. I would give 0 stars if possible. Note to CNLPRO: I have extensive written and visual proof, as well as saved WhatsApp conversations, to back up every single one of these claims.

Issue details
The Endesa On York Way app, which requires installation, registration, and adding a payment method, is by far the worst—slow and unreliable. There are four 22kW charging points, two of which are out of service. I connected to one of the available ones after the cumbersome app registration process, but after five minutes, it told me the charging had stopped. I returned to the parking lot and saw one of the 60kW charging points was free (the other was occupied and connected, but not charging; it probably couldn't complete the session). With the app, I couldn't end the charging session on the 22kW point no matter how many times I tried; it didn't give an error message, it just wouldn't complete. I had to report a problem, and they closed it shortly after. However, the €15 pre-authorization on my card was processed correctly. I did manage to complete the charging session on the 22kW point. To connect to the 60kW charger, since one slot was occupied and not charging, there was no way to know which slot was free. The charging station wasn't numbered, the app didn't indicate anything, and even the QR code didn't work because the app then asked me to choose one... It was a complete mess. Finally—and quite randomly—I managed to connect and charge. Result: Time spent waiting to start charging ~30 min.

one_star_reviews.text:
After waiting so many days, my case being highly urgent, I was referred from Severo Ochoa Hospital in Leganés due to a dangerous spike in blood pressure at work—it was very high, reaching 118—and swelling of my lower lip, possibly from poisoning or an allergic reaction to medication. I was taken by ambulance to Severo Ochoa Hospital in Leganés, where I received excellent professional care. I was in the emergency room from morning until the early hours.

I received an appointment for an allergy specialist at the Red Cross Hospital and arrived half an hour early, on June 17, 2026, at 8:30 a.m., hoping to be seen at 9:00 a.m. I notified the nurse of my arrival, and she told me to leave because the doctor scheduled to see me wouldn't be coming due to a strike. I told her I had arrived half an hour before my appointment and would wait until 9:00 or 9:15. She insisted I shouldn't wait because she wouldn't suddenly appear. The head of the Allergy Unit overheard the conversation, actually speaking in a respectful tone, unlike the nurse. He encouraged me to wait until my appointment time. The appointment arrived, and after about 15 minutes, the head of the unit came out again and told me to leave, that the doctor wouldn't be coming, and that I should go downstairs to schedule another appointment for another day.

I asked the head of the Allergy Department why they hadn't notified me not to come in, since the doctor has the right to strike. I've had to lose work hours, which affects the company I work for in Leganés, and I've lost money on transportation. They told me that by law they can't notify me that the doctor won't be coming, unless they refer me to another doctor who is seeing patients. To save me all this trouble, I think that during all strikes they maintain some minimum service, or they could refer me to an emergency room to get the priority allergy tests I've been told to get.

I don't know much about the law, but I believe there are good professionals in the public healthcare system; the problem lies with the administration. When it comes to tests that a doctor designates as priority, that's when they take the longest, and months can go by before you're seen. Now I have to wait until August to get my priority allergy test.

I believe we can prevent this harm to people, the despair and distress of knowing you're ill and the professionals who are supposed to prolong our lives can't help you because they have to exercise their right to protest for better working conditions.

We, the relatives, are the ones who pay for all these problems with our health.

I ask the legislators to please legislate with the understanding that they, too, are human beings who can get sick at any time. Doctors work to extend our lives; we must take care of them and keep them happy, as well as those of us who work to maintain the public healthcare system.

The worst staff I have ever encountered at a parking garage.

The employee at the entrance spent the entire time on a video call on his phone instead of paying attention to customers. When I arrived, he didn't even notice I was there. This was one of the most unprofessional customer service experiences I have ever had. I came there intending to rent a parking space for several months, but after being treated like this, I would never leave my car there. one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with this official dealership was terrible. Be very careful with them.

I took my 2021 Jeep Renegade (109,000 km) in for a diagnostic check, and after charging me €393, I was informed that the engine was seized and that there were "possibly" other additional problems. The diagnosis itself was based on expressions like "possibly" or "it would have to be checked by disassembling it," without a clear and definitive technical conclusion.

The worst part isn't the €393 they charged (just for a diagnosis). The worst part is that an owner who receives a seized engine diagnosis might start to think their vehicle has reached the end of its useful life. Had I fully trusted that diagnosis, I could have made an irreversible decision, like selling the car for scrap or getting rid of it for a ridiculously low price, convinced that the engine was beyond repair.

Fortunately, I decided to get a second opinion and took the vehicle to another garage. There, they verified that the engine was NOT seized, managed to start it, and subsequently carried out the necessary repairs, providing documentation that the engine was functioning correctly.

Furthermore, when I picked up the vehicle from this official workshop, they returned it to me with disassembled parts inside, something I consider unacceptable for a professional service.

After presenting them with videos, technical explanations from the mechanic, the invoice for the subsequent repair, and all the documentation proving that the engine was working, they finally refunded me €300 of the €393 initially charged.

Each reader can draw their own conclusions. I can only say that I have completely lost confidence in this workshop.

I have emails, photographs, videos, the diagnostic invoice, the invoice for the subsequent repair, and all the necessary documentation to prove each of the facts described in this review.

When I broke up with my ex-partner, he came to me with a document to vacate the apartment because the owner wanted to evict me. Of course, he wanted to sign a new contract for a higher monthly rent with Erlantz, who had already started his own agency, stealing all of Olatz's clients. He even made me sign a document even though he no longer worked for Olatz, the agency with which I had the rental agreement. All this so he could earn his commission on the new rental. Well, Erlantz, you should know that karma will come back to you. Your employees will steal your clients and start their own agencies with your business. I don't think anyone likes this, but it's really told me a lot: you only think about yourself and don't care about others.

So, if I were to sell my apartment or want to buy one, based solely on who this person is, I wouldn't do any business with him.

one_star_reviews.text:
We decided to stop at this restaurant because of the views and because the place looked nice. However, the experience was quite disappointing.

We ordered two beers (more than €4 each) and, for our young daughters, we asked for glasses of tap water. At that moment, we sensed a rather uncomfortable attitude from the staff, as if asking for tap water was a problem, especially since we were talking about children. To avoid any argument, we ended up ordering a small bottle of water for more than €3.

It's worth remembering that, since the entry into force of Law 7/2022, of April 8, hospitality establishments in Spain must offer consumers the option of drinking tap water free of charge and as an addition to their menu. That's why we were particularly surprised by the staff's attitude toward such a simple request.

With that feeling, we decided to order only two dishes, as the atmosphere didn't encourage us to stay any longer. We also got the impression that they were surprised we ordered so little food, but we simply weren't comfortable anymore and continued because we were already seated.

We ordered a portion of fried calamari: €17 for 7 pieces, with nothing to justify that price, as they were just ordinary calamari, like you can find in many other places for much less. We also ordered mussels marinara, which were very good, although €17 seemed expensive for the amount served.

In short, the views are beautiful, but the service and the value for money made the experience unsatisfactory. We don't recommend it and we won't be back.

It's not normal to wait around for a while, looking to see if anyone's attending to you, and then, when you don't see anyone, go in to use the restroom and are asked in a very rude tone where you're going, and told you're rude and should have asked permission. Restrooms are for public use, mandatory for everyone, no matter how much many places insist they're only for customers, which is completely illegal. With that kind of welcome, I predict great success for this restaurant.

My experience with this company has been very negative. After paying a significant amount of money for the contracted work, they left the job unfinished and failed to complete the agreed-upon work.

In addition to missing deadlines and leaving the project incomplete, much of the work done was of poor quality and contained numerous errors that had to be corrected later. A project that was initially scheduled to last two months dragged on for more than six months, causing significant inconvenience and damage.

Furthermore, during the execution of the work, various damages were caused to the property, which, despite being reported repeatedly, were neither repaired nor taken responsibility for by the company.

To top it all off, they were unprofessional and, on several occasions, rude when I asked them for a solution. Overall, I felt a complete lack of responsibility, seriousness, and commitment to the client. I would not recommend this company at all!

I was supposed to have a washing machine delivered, and I received a message indicating the delivery window and that they would notify me 30 minutes before arriving at my address.

However, on the day of the delivery, they only called me 8 minutes before arriving. At that time, I was at work, about 15 minutes from home. When I explained my situation, the delivery driver was very unprofessional and quite rude. His exact words were: “I’ll wait 5 minutes. If you don’t show up in that time, I’m leaving.” He also denied that I had been informed that I would receive a 30-minute notification.

I finally managed to arrive on time because a colleague lent me a bicycle. The driver, with whom I had spoken on the phone, didn’t even get out of the van.

Later, I sent him a WhatsApp message to the same number he had called me from repeatedly (about six times, trying to hurry me up), attaching a screenshot of the message that clearly stated the 30-minute notification. His response was two audio messages in which he told me not to be reckless, not to text that number again because it was his personal phone, and that he was going to report me.

And this raises a question that I find very worrying: how does this company manage its customers' personal data? Why would a delivery driver use his personal phone number to contact customers during a delivery? Besides the way I was treated, I believe this situation raises serious concerns about the company's privacy practices and data protection.

Because I can't give a lower rating.

I placed an order with IKEA where I could choose a delivery time slot. I selected 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM because I wasn't home and my parents, who live an hour away, could travel with enough time to receive the order without any problem.

However, at 3:00 PM, one of the delivery drivers called my mother saying they were already there and that if they didn't arrive immediately, they would leave. The tone and manner were completely unacceptable. During the drive, my mother received three more calls pressuring them to arrive as soon as possible, so they had to rush, with all the stress and worry that entails, especially considering her age.

The most surprising thing is that when my parents arrived at 4:16 PM, the delivery drivers had already brought all the merchandise up to the landing without anyone there to receive it. If the delivery was scheduled between 5:00 PM and 9:00 PM, it's incomprehensible that they showed up two hours early and, moreover, expected the customer to be available immediately.

To make matters worse, they marked the order as delivered around 5:46 PM, when I can prove, thanks to my alarm record, that everything happened much earlier.

I want to make it clear that my complaint is not against IKEA. The service I received from the company was good, and they responded appropriately to my issue. My dissatisfaction is solely with the delivery company and the attitude of its employees. I sincerely hope that IKEA reviews its partnership with this supplier and that, if they don't change their way of working and treating customers, they stop using them.

I hope no one else has to go through the stressful and disrespectful situation my parents experienced.

I wish they had a zero-star rating.

I've known companies with poor management, poor organization, or poor customer service, but this one has them all and far surpasses them.

I bought an American-style refrigerator and a washing machine. From the moment of purchase, I explicitly stated that the refrigerator wouldn't fit in the elevator, something I communicated in advance.

The delivery was scheduled for June 3rd. That day, the delivery driver, Edilberto, arrived at the building with the appliances, asked which floor the delivery was to, and upon discovering it was the fourth floor and that the refrigerator wouldn't fit in the elevator, stated that the appliance was too heavy and he wouldn't bring it up. He left without offering any solution. Minutes later, I received a text message indicating that the delivery couldn't be made due to "force majeure."

Without consulting me, the delivery was rescheduled for June 8th. At 10:30 a.m., another delivery driver arrived to measure the elevator again, even though this information had already been communicated numerous times. After taking the measurements, he told me he would return in a couple of hours with a support team to carry the refrigerator up the stairs.

I waited all day. No one showed up. No one called. No one informed me of any changes.

Finally, after 8:30 p.m., I received another text message stating that the delivery could not be made due to issues on the route and that it was automatically rescheduled for June 11th.

The worst part of this whole situation is not only the lack of organization, but the absolute lack of respect for the customer's time. I have had to rearrange my schedule and work obligations several times to receive a delivery that never arrives. The company unilaterally reschedules dates and expects the customer to continue adapting indefinitely.

Communication is practically nonexistent, and obtaining information or solutions is extremely difficult.

For my part, I will be filing the corresponding complaints with the Consumer Protection Agency and exploring the appropriate legal action for the damages caused.

My experience has been deeply disappointing, and I would not recommend this service to anyone.

Yesterday we went to this restaurant and saw that the portion of calamari fritters cost €14.90.

After ordering, we waited 1 hour and 10 minutes for our food. When we asked the waiter what was happening, instead of apologizing for the delay or explaining it politely, he responded quite rudely, saying that they first had to serve a paella for a large group. His manner left much to be desired.

When the calamari finally arrived, frankly, we weren't impressed. It seemed like it had been cooked hastily and carelessly.

The worst part came when we paid. The menu listed €14.90, but they charged us €18.90. When we asked why, they said the menu was outdated and that the correct price was the one on the website. I replied that I hadn't looked at the website, but rather at the menu they themselves had given me, and that the logical thing to do was to charge the price listed there. Their response was simply no.

Furthermore, their manner of replying was quite rude. At no point did they apologize for the wait or the pricing error. When I told them I was going to take a picture of the menu to leave a review, they replied that the restaurant didn't live off reviews. I found this response very unprofessional and disrespectful to a customer who had been polite throughout.

I was passing through Albacete and had to return to Madrid, so I couldn't waste any more time filing a complaint. That's why I paid and decided to share my experience here.

Honestly, I don't think this restaurant is worth it. A bad experience both because of the wait and the service I received. I've attached photos so you can see the difference between the price listed on the menu and what they ultimately charged me.

We had been here on other occasions and had always left happy, so we were so surprised by what happened last night.

The waiters were attentive throughout, and as a nice touch, they offered us some desserts, which we appreciated. However, that doesn't make up for the terrible experience we had with the food.

The croquettes had a sour taste, as if they were spoiled, and we also found hairs and small insects in several dishes, which is completely unacceptable from a hygiene standpoint. We reported this and decided to leave a review detailing our experience. To our surprise, as we were leaving the restaurant, an employee came to demand the review instead of showing any concern about what had happened or apologizing.

To make matters worse, several people in our group woke up today with stomach problems and diarrhea, which is worrying after having dinner there.

It's a shame because it was a place we had been to before and that we liked, but last night's experience was awful.

We hope they will review both food preservation and hygiene measures to prevent this from happening again.

Our experience was quite bad. We ordered a Spanish omelet and found a hair in it. There were also several mosquitoes on the omelet itself, which we found completely unacceptable from a hygiene standpoint.

We also ordered some porcini mushroom croquettes that had a sour, vinegary taste, so we didn't trust them at all and could barely eat them.

The bread was rock hard, seemed several days old, and was very difficult to eat.

To top it all off, when the desserts arrived, we had to wait about 20 minutes for even simple spoons, so the desserts sat on the table for practically that entire time.

On the positive side, we have to acknowledge that the waiters reacted well. As soon as we told them what had happened, they replaced the food without any fuss, didn't charge us for the omelet, and even gave us some complimentary desserts as compensation, in addition to the ones we had already ordered. That gesture and the staff's service were good.

Even so, no matter how hard the staff tried to fix the problem, finding a hair and mosquitoes in the food, in addition to being served croquettes with a distinctly sour taste, are things that should never happen in a restaurant.
To top it all off, they came to reprimand us for leaving a negative review, which we found completely inappropriate.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm writing this review as the buyer who purchased a safe driving course on January 31st as a gift for my partner. For whatever reason, she wasn't given an appointment until today, June 28th, at 2:00 PM, right in the middle of a heatwave. I couldn't accompany her, but I've had to endure this whole ordeal on the other end of the phone, providing emotional support, with utter helplessness.

Since the RACC (Royal Automobile Club of Catalonia) indicates in its instructions that there's the option of walking (warning that it's a 45-minute walk), she took public transport. The problem is the company's complete lack of judgment: for an organization that supposedly sells "safety" to propose a 45-minute walk in the blazing sun, at 2:00 PM in the summer, and during a heatwave as a viable alternative is reckless. It's an obvious danger to anyone's health, especially when the entire logistics surrounding the circuit fail spectacularly:
- Fake access points: The buses that are supposed to run never showed up. The taxi phones at the station weren't working (they told her they were having lunch).

- Complete abandonment: She had to walk alone in 35°C heat for 45 minutes on a route with practically no shade. To make matters worse, the pedestrian path was blocked by a construction sign, and she had to go around it to keep moving.

- Lack of communication: They don't provide any direct contact number for the RACC or the Montmeló center to call if you're running late due to these unforeseen circumstances or if you need emergency directions.

- Lack of information at the circuit: She had to get a taxi at the last minute in the final meters while she called me crying, sunburned and on the verge of heatstroke. To top it all off, since the taxi driver didn't know where the RACC center was either, he dropped her off on the other side of the circuit. There, nobody could give her directions, and there's no RACC staff to assist you until you're physically inside their building. On a Sunday afternoon, the circuit is a deserted place with no information.

She'll surely leave her own review later to detail whether this whole ordeal is somehow compensated by the course. For my part, as a customer who paid for a service and ended up listening to my partner suffer through a nightmare on the phone due to the company's complete lack of foresight and irresponsibility, I'm certain that unless things change drastically, I'll never again give anything from this company as a gift or recommend them to anyone. It's deplorable.

one_star_reviews.text:
My wife and I went to the dealership to inquire about an electric Renault 5 for my commute. While talking to the salesperson, we asked about the Alpine version, and coincidentally, they had a demonstrator model for sale, license plate 3874-MYM, for €34,500.
The salesperson told us that only the dealership manager had ever used that car. After several days of deliberation, we decided the Alpine model suited us. We went to make a reservation and paid a €500 deposit while we arranged financing. Imagine my surprise that same evening when I saw several videos on YouTube and TikTok of the car we had reserved, and we verified that it was indeed the same one because it had the same license plate, 3874-MYM. I felt ripped off! Then, the car that, according to the dealership, had only been used by the manager, turned out to be a test car for motoring magazines. We saw track tests of that exact same car.

After demanding a refund of the €500 we had paid for a demonstrator car (not a test car), they deigned to make us an offer deducting €1,500 + VAT from the initial price and a letter taking responsibility for any hidden defects. I don't know if that letter included taking responsibility for thinking buyers are idiots. A demonstrator car is not the same as a test car.
We made them a counteroffer deducting €5,000, which they were within their rights to reject, but they still wouldn't refund our money. A week later, and under threat of filing a complaint with the Civil Guard (magic words) and the Consumers' Association, they finally returned our money.
We will continue looking for another electric car, but it's clear it won't be a Renault. Not so much because the car was a test car, but because we think they might try to rip off their potential customers.
I'm sharing links to the videos we found, in case they block them.

What a shame!!!! I tried to post the video links but they won't let me. You can search for them by typing "Alpine A290 GTS test" and you'll find several.

My experience was very disappointing.

I bought a dress for €70 at their pop-up shop in Madrid, specifically @popupconceptmadrid right in the heart of Goya. Just a day later, I found the exact same garment at a bazaar for €23. Obviously, this made me question the true value of the product I had bought, so I went back to the pop-up shop to ask for an explanation and, above all, to get my money back.

What bothered me most wasn't just the huge price difference, but the response I received. Instead of understanding my surprise and frustration as a customer, they simply justified the situation by saying that many garments come from the same suppliers and that this happens with many brands. At no point did they acknowledge that a customer might feel cheated when they discover that a garment sold in a boutique for €70 can be found exactly the same for less than a third of that price.

Furthermore, at first they refused to refund my money and only offered me a voucher to spend again in the store. Only when I suggested requesting a formal complaint form did they change their stance and agree to the refund.

I finally got my money back, but I left with a very unpleasant feeling. More than the dress itself, I was disappointed by the lack of empathy and the way they handled a completely reasonable complaint.

My advice for future shoppers is simple: compare prices before buying here. After my experience, I would recommend looking first in the local bazaars and shops, because you might find the exact same product for much less money, and in a shop right next door.

I will not be shopping at this establishment again. And if you do, check the local bazaars first.

A regrettable experience yesterday at the Spain-Belgium match of the 2026 World Cup.

First, you arrive and have to pay an entrance fee if you're on the terrace. It's €10 for adults with two drinks and €5 for children with one drink. The shocking thing is that if you have a reservation inside, you don't have to pay an entrance fee; you only pay if you're on the terrace! Then there are the drinks. They gave you a 0.33-liter beer in a cardboard cup. If you ordered it inside, it was €3 per beer, and you could get a glass. So, if you were outside, the same beer that came with the drink you paid for upon entry cost you €5, €2 more than if you had a reservation inside.

Inside, there was a menu with a wider variety of burgers for €14, while on the terrace, there was a different, basic menu of burgers and hot dogs for €16. When you asked the staff, they told you it was the same inside as outside, which wasn't true. It wasn't the same menu or the same price, but if you ordered inside, you couldn't take it out to the terrace yourself.

Not to mention that we had to wait because they had forgotten to set our table despite our advance reservation, and they hadn't informed us in the reservation that there was an entrance fee that included a drink.

The speakers weren't loud enough for the number of people there; you couldn't hear anything!

For this reason, we won't be attending any important events at this bar again.

Our experience organizing an event for over 25 female entrepreneurs was disappointing.

Before confirming the meeting, we inquired about the venue's conditions and were told that we could hold the event without a minimum spend requirement and with a specific room layout. Based on this information, we began all the planning.

However, some time later, we were informed of new conditions that hadn't been mentioned initially, including the requirement to order a set menu per person and limitations on the use of the space. This forced us to rethink part of the organization with very little time to spare.

The most unpleasant aspect wasn't the conditions themselves, since any establishment is free to set its own rules, but rather the way they were communicated. During the conversation, the manager, Julie, repeatedly stated things like "I'm the one in charge here" and that she set the conditions, creating an unprofessional and customer-centric impression.

We understand that businesses have their own rules, but we believe that transparency, clarity from the outset, and respectful treatment are essential, especially when organizing an event for more than 25 people.

Unfortunately, our experience did not meet our expectations.

We made a reservation well in advance and specifically requested a low table on the terrace, or at least a low table inside if that wasn't possible. We felt that if they couldn't guarantee this, they should have informed us beforehand.

Upon arrival, we were not only rudely informed that there would be no terrace, but we were also seated at a small, uncomfortable table, practically next to other customers, with chairs in poor condition. The staff's treatment was unpleasant and unprofessional throughout, making us feel uncomfortable from the moment we arrived.

Furthermore, given that this is the bar of a sports club like RCD Mallorca, we believe they should pay much more attention to customer service and courtesy. The image projected by a place associated with the club should be up to par, and frankly, the experience was very disappointing.

We understand that there may be space limitations or organizational changes, but what is unacceptable is the lack of attention, empathy, and courtesy towards customers who had booked in advance and clearly specified their needs.

The experience has been very disappointing and completely different from what was expected.
